lesson: When `--debug-model` is supplied with `--skip jira-intake`, the debugger cannot run (no TicketSpec). Either auto-include jira-intake whenever `--debug-model` is set, or pause the debugger with a clear NEEDS_INPUT message naming the missing dependency.
evidence: EDAEM-3772 debug attempt returned None silently; the supervisor needs to surface the missing precondition instead of swallowing it.

lesson: Two-mode dispatcher: Mode A (scheduled - delegates to ARRCloseOrchestrator core) and Mode B (ticket-driven 10-role DAG). Mode-resolution rule: ticket only -> Mode B; as_was_date only -> Mode A; both -> Mode B then a snapshot rebuild. --quarter-close always routes through Mode B so the on-demand quarter-close-runner gets dispatched (with its thinking-log entry + recon matrix).

Canonical DAG order: jira-intake -> requirements-analyzer -> code-data-validator -> clarifier -> implementer -> test-runner -> pr-author -> ci-monitor -> cd-monitor -> qa-handoff. Debugger and quarter-close-runner are on-demand (NOT in the canonical tuple) - dispatched via auto-on-FAIL, Slack `task:` side-channel, or CLI (--debug-model / --quarter-close).

Recognized side-channel commands (Slack `task:` prefix): skip, pause, cancel, status, debug, quarter-close. Anything else is queued as a free-form side task and surfaced in the final report so a human or the Cursor coding agent can pick it up later. Polling cursor is `last_side_channel_ts` on SupervisorState - resume-safe.

Debug-on-failure is ON by default - whenever any role returns FAIL, the debugger auto-dispatches BEFORE the supervisor pauses, so the operator sees a debug bundle alongside the pause point. Disable with --no-debug-on-failure. The debugger needs a TicketSpec from jira-intake - never auto-skip jira-intake when --debug-model is set.

Clarifier interactive timeout defaults to 600s. When clarifier returns NEEDS_INPUT, the supervisor surfaces the questions on stdin and waits; on timeout (or non-tty), falls back to pause-and-post to Jira. Set --clarifier-interactive-timeout 0 (or --no-clarifier-interactive) for unattended runs to skip straight to Jira.

EDADEV cross-ticket dependency pattern: when a refactor needs GTM-side SCD2 column enablement (or any upstream platform change), file an EDADEV ticket and link it as a blocker on the EDAEM ticket. Template: clone EDADEV-2861 / EDAEM-3411. The supervisor should refuse to mark the EDAEM ticket Ready-for-QA until the EDADEV dependency is Resolved.
evidence: Refactored QA / UAT Testing - separate ref() for stg_em_agreement_line_item_scd2 blocked on EDADEV-2861.

lesson: `ans:` answer->question mapping strategy: (1) numbered split of a single combined reply like '1) x 2) y'; (2) positional when N ans: lines == N questions; (3) combined fallback attaching the whole reply to the first question with pointers on the rest. Always clear answered questions from requirements.questions so downstream roles don't re-ask.

Before reporting any QoQ ARR variance, decompose it into (a) FX/constant-currency reset, (b) logic deploy, (c) data corrections/migrations, and check the ED&A release notes. Most ad-hoc AI 'variances' are really FX resets, migrations, or announced logic changes - not bugs.

Scope boundary: ED&A calculates ARR from the source-of-record and does NOT verify source accuracy. Never claim a source data error - frame as 'this source value drives the result; route to RevRec/Remediation'. ED&A also does not do ad-hoc outlier research during close without account/agreement IDs + a real suspected logic gap.
